title: Quantum Rényi-Jarzynski Equality
authors: Benjamin Bobell, Mert Okyay, Rahul Nandkishore
abstract: The Jarzynski equality provides a strict link between nonequilibrium work and equilibrium free energy changes. Its typical quantum formulations, however, rely on measurement protocols that destroy coherence. In this Letter, we use the resource-theoretic approach to derive a non-destructive quantum Jarzynski equality conditioned on the outcomes of an arbitrary bath observable. This yields the Rényi-Jarzynski equality, which quantifies a finite bath's drift from equilibrium under a non-adiabatic drive via the Rényi $k$-divergence. We further demonstrate that the Rényi-Jarzynski equality provides a tunable cost function for quantum optimal control problems where minimizing bath drift is desired, such as state preparation and gate design, enabling the minimization of cross-talk in finite quantum systems. Our toy model exhibits a transition between competing minima for some critical value of $k$, illustrating how the Rényi order tunes sensitivity to different regions of a bath distribution. Strikingly, when drive parameters vary across bath energy levels, minimizing bath drift requires generating system-bath entanglement.
summary: This paper introduces the Rényi-Jarzynski Equality, a generalized fluctuation theorem that links non-equilibrium work to free energy changes using the Rényi $k$-divergence. It overcomes measurement limitations by conditioning the equality on bath observable outcomes. The resulting divergence acts as a tunable cost function, enabling the minimization of bath drift in quantum optimal control and revealing entanglement generation requirements.
main_problem: To derive a non-destructive quantum Jarzynski equality (Rényi-Jarzynski Equality) that links nonequilibrium work to equilibrium free energy changes, overcoming limitations of standard quantum formulations.
main_result: The RJE quantifies bath drift using the Rényi $k$-divergence, providing a tunable cost function for quantum optimal control problems.
method: The authors employ a resource-theoretic approach, deriving fluctuation theorems conditioned on arbitrary bath observable outcomes, leading to the generalized Rényi-Jarzynski equality.
model_or_system: The analysis uses a tripartite setup (System-Bath-Weight) and extends to toy models involving $d$-state qudits, analyzing the dynamics under non-adiabatic driving.
key_observables: Rényi $k$-divergence ($D_k(P_0||P_f)$), Bath Drift, Work ($W$), and Free Energy Change ($\Delta F_S$).
important_parameters: The Rényi order $k$, the bath dimension $d$, and the drive parameters ($	heta$).
main_assumptions: The derivation is conditioned on the outcomes of an arbitrary bath observable, and some analyses rely on quasi-classical approximations or dropping coherence terms when calculating bath marginals.
figures_summary: Not specified, but the text describes the derivation of several numbered equations (1) through (18) representing core results.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the general non-destructive quantum Jarzynski equality, to generalizing this to $k$-th moments and the Rényi divergence, and finally applying this metric to analyze optimal control problems in toy qudit models.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, generalized thermodynamic constraint (the RJE) that moves beyond standard fluctuation theorems by incorporating the Rényi divergence, making it highly relevant for designing robust quantum control protocols.
